question: Can the known speed/load regime of completed source devices be recognized from the current 34 legal vibration fields, well enough to correct differently signed timing errors on a new device? Source metadata supplies training-only regime labels, taken from the original upstream source folder. Deployment never receives device, regime, age or later samples. Existing external published backgrounds are used for transfer stress; these are development runs.
sources: The general input-dependent expert principle is from Jacobs et al., Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts (1991). Source-condition supervision, nearest-centroid ridge-discriminant with equal device weighting and writing smooth one-versus-rest gates into otherwise unchanged hidden units are project adaptations. Official B TASK.md gives the two-axis feature contract, the authors' XJTU-SY data expressly group bearings by operating setting. There are nine source devices, three per condition. Do not infer an exact lifetime from knowing the operating condition.
models: Use only original official weights, 34-feature source normalizer and the existing 24 tanh units. Source-only balanced design with two budgets: 72 existing fit rows and all 7032 source rows, always equal total weight per device. Train an LDA on normalized observed features for the three source conditions, within-class covariance shrunk halfway to its diagonal; default all three equally likely. Out-of-device regime classification checked by leave-one-source-device-out with classifier normalization fitted from that fold only. On actual service report accuracy only when true XJTU condition is known, for diagnosis after prediction. Freeze comparison against global equal-device mean lifetime residual and fixed base, fixed training median, and existing native tree-hidden checkpoint. Correcting the residual: for each source condition learn the mean error y minus parent prediction with equal-device weights, and soft/hard condition classifier predicts this added error. Compare an external gate with a single official weight implementation: leave all but the three least-contributing source hidden units untouched; for each condition take one tanh of its discriminant score minus the arithmetic mean of the other two, scale by source standard deviation of that contrast, then fit the three new output weights and intercept by weighted ridge (.001 regularization per unit total data mass in normalized target units) keeping all other original output weights fixed. Matched source-budget controls replace the same three slots by their untouched original features then fit the same coefficients, and permute regime labels cyclically across devices within ordered source replicates (not a global class renaming). Anchor optional front-end analysis with true-condition at evaluation only on XJTU. Keep out-of-device site stress separate from official interface. Model-byte hashes, CPU, training identities and adverse devices recorded.
adoption: Actual single-weight candidate evaluated before later-device labels. A candidate remains eligible for normal-entry verification only with >=1 percent pooled RMSE improvement versus both current and same-budget unchanged-slot control on the official service assignment and all official role assignments, <=1 percent worst-unit increase versus both, and no deterioration >1 percent over current at the other XJTU and PRONOSTIA sites. Also report strongest fixed reference on every site. If no candidate meets this criterion, reject regime correction for default. Do not fit a new gate threshold from those results; separate whether recognition fails or even providing the true condition cannot correct the varying lifespans within it.
